name: Francis Parra
home: the blocks north of the port
life: “I still remember trying to put on an apron over my shareholder's coat.” People around the courtyard by Ferry Street Rooms know Francis by a small Saturday habit. Francis prefers the bench where the sound of the shop door reaches before the visitor does.
voice: I have shares and no apron. I offered to carry flour for one afternoon before looking at the daily numbers.
appearance: Francis has heavy brows and an unusually delicate jaw. Look for steel-colored hair cut square above the collar. Away from the heat of the kitchen, the familiar outfit is a soft blue checked shirt with a cloth patch so neatly matched it only shows in strong light. In conversation Francis takes off the watch before a long conversation.
personality: Francis loves a well-told anecdote and distrusts the neat ending. The parts Francis remembers are the interruptions, unfinished jobs and people who had to go back to work halfway through.
agenda: To put real flour-handling time behind a shareholder opinion.
family: Talia Valdez is Francis’s stepsibling. Francis is allowed to ask about the bad news afterward. Talia calls about good news first. Neither wants every family conversation to begin with a bill, a diagnosis or an apology. Asked about *The pawned trumpet*, Talia says, “I taught two pupils on that horn. Neither ever knew I owned it first.”
connections: Teal Aranda. Carrying flour changes what a shareholder is prepared to say about the workers' rota.

reactions.situation: Two kitchen workers disagree on the new shift rota
reactions.response: Francis puts both proposed rotas beside the actual delivery and childcare times.
